name: Covered Put
summary: Short 100 shares and sell a put against the short position - the bearish mirror of a covered call, capping the downside gain and leaving unlimited upside risk.
max_profit: (short share price - put strike + credit) x 100
max_loss: UNDEFINED - unlimited as the stock rises, because the short shares are unhedged above
when_to_use: Bearish-to-neutral view where the system wants to collect premium on a short stock position. FLAGGED: requires short stock and, at most brokers, level 4; the unlimited upside risk plus borrow and dividend obligations make it a poor fit for an automated share-settled account.
entry_rules: BLOCKED at level 3 - short stock plus a short put is treated as an uncovered position for approval purposes at most brokers; verify Alpaca's specific treatment before enabling, and assume level 4.
If enabled: require a confirmed borrow, borrow rate < 3% annualized, and no dividend inside the option's life (the short seller owes it).
Standard premium gates: IVR >= 30, credit >= 1% of strike notional, OI >= 250.
Mandatory stop on the share leg: buy to cover if spot > entry x 1.10.
management_rules: 50% profit target on the put; 21 DTE roll.
Roll the put up-and-out for a credit if the stock falls and the put goes deep ITM.
Hard risk control: the short stock leg must carry a stop - this structure has no natural upside defense.
exit_rules: HARD: flatten the short put by 15:30 ET on expiration day if ITM. Assignment delivers 100 LONG shares, which closes the short stock - benign in isolation but unplanned.
Close the put when extrinsic < 0.05 and delta < -0.85.
Close the whole unit (buy to cover shares + buy to close put) as one combo on any upside stop trigger.
assignment_risk: The short put is assignable; assignment buys 100 shares that close the short position at the strike, which is actually the intended max-profit outcome, but it happens at a time of the counterparty's choosing. The uncontrolled risk is not assignment, it is the naked upside on the short shares and the dividend/buy-in obligations.
buying_power: Reg-T short stock margin (150% of proceeds) plus the put requirement. Level 4.
liquidity_needs: Borrowable name with a liquid put chain.
common_mistakes: Treating it as symmetric with a covered call - it is not: the covered call's worst case is owning a cheap stock, the covered put's worst case is unlimited.
family: Stock/ETF Shares Combined With Options (covered writes, protective hedges, collars, synthetics, repairs, conversions)
blocked_because: needs Alpaca options level 4; this account is level 3. Alpaca rejects it with 'account not eligible to trade uncovered option contracts'. Raising the level is an Alpaca approval, not a code change.
